messages:
Claire (CS): FYI customer case #5471 reporting retrieval/ranking quality drop after our rollout. They say citations are missing and answers are hallucinating more often. Started right after this morning's release.

Mateo (ML): Can you paste a minimal repro (query + expected vs actual) and the request payload? Also which model/retriever config they were pinned to?

Claire (CS): Quick repro from customer (redacted):

Request: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"Find latest clinical guidance on post-op infection control for total knee arthroplasty","retrieval":true,"retriever_config":{"index":"customer-acmemed-v1","top_k":8}}'

Actual (snippet): "The current guidance recommends routine prophylactic antibiotics and telemonitoring. [no citation]"
Expected: Citations to NICE guidance and a specific journal review (customer had those docs in their index).

Customer note: "This used to return 3-4 direct doc citations in the answer; now we get generic language and no doc refs." They attached two examples.

eng-oncall-bot: deploy-bot posted: deployed service=ranking-service tag=ranker-v3 release_id=2026-03-15T09:10:05Z by @ci-cd (rollout=50%)

Priya (Infra): Do we have any spike in error or latency around 09:10 UTC for the customer's tenant? Could be partial rollout causing inconsistent reranks. I'll pull edge logs for tenant acmemed.

Mateo (ML): Two quick hypotheses: 1) the reranker weight default in the pipeline changed (more weight to dense-sim => fewer doc citations surfaced), 2) a retrieval index mismatch (embedding dims or new encoder). Claire, can you confirm if the customer was on the default pipeline or had an explicit pipeline override?

Claire (CS): They were on the default pipeline and hadn't changed routing. Customer timestamp for first bad response: 2026-03-15T09:12:34Z (exactly after the rollout).

Mateo (ML): Please run this internal quick check against their index to compare scores pre/post: 

```
python infra/tools/rerank_eval.py --tenant acmemed --queries samples/clinical-ops.json --snapshot-before 2026-03-15T09:00:00Z --snapshot-after 2026-03-15T09:15:00Z --topk 8
```

This will dump retrieval hits + reranker scores. If reranker top candidates have lower relevance after rollout, that's our culprit. Also check config file `/configs/pipeline_defaults/ranking_weights.json` — I suspect the "rerank_weight" got changed.

Priya (Infra): I pulled edge logs for tenant acmemed: no 5xx spikes, latency stable. But I do see traffic routed to a new ranking cluster `ranker-v3` starting at 09:10:05Z for ~52% of requests (matches deploy-bot).

Mateo (ML): Thanks. If ranker-v3 is the new model, it may have different calibration. Quick mitigation options: 1) rollback rollout to 0% for ranker-v3, 2) apply temporary config override to increase doc-pref weight (rerank_weight up to 0.9), 3) disable dense-only fallback. Claire, customer is asking for urgent rollback if repro confirms.

Claire (CS): Customer impact: high — several production users rely on doc citations. They want a rollback if we confirm regression. Please treat P1.

Jordan (CS Manager): Marking this P1 and tagging Product/Release. @Mateo, @Priya, please coordinate rollback plan. Will notify customer that we're investigating and may do rollback within the hour. :eyes:

Mateo (ML): I'll run rerank_eval now and paste diffs. If results show mean reciprocal rank drop > 0.25 we'll recommend rollback.

Claire (CS): Running the customer's failing example through a staging call for reference: 

```
POST /v1/chat
{ "input":"Find latest clinical guidance on post-op infection control for total knee arthroplasty","retrieval":true }
```

Staging reply (pre-rollout snapshot): contains doc ids [doc: NICE-2024-guideline, doc: JClinReview-2023] with spans.

Staging reply (post-rollout snapshot): generic summary, no doc ids.

Mateo (ML): Eval output (summary): MRR before=0.68, after=0.31; top doc overlap before/after=37%. Reranker score distributions show mean score downshift for relevant docs in ranker-v3. Config diff shows {"rerank_weight":0.6} in v3 vs {"rerank_weight":0.85} in v2.

Mateo (ML): Recommend rollback to ranker-v2 and a follow-up A/B with corrected weights. I'll open an internal release ticket.

Priya (Infra): Rolling back rollout flag now to route 100% -> ranker-v2. Deploy-bot: rollout update service=ranking-service set rollouts=ranker-v3:0,ranker-v2:100 by @Priya (Infra) at 2026-03-15T09:23:10Z

Claire (CS): Customer updated: "Thanks, we see citations again — seems fixed." They will monitor for 2 hours and update.

Jordan (CS Manager): Good work team. Please capture root cause (config drift in packaging) and add to postmortem. I'll create incident ticket INC-2026-045.

Mateo (ML): I'll also add regression tests to the pre-release suite that check citation recall on a small set of tenant indices (sanity check for reranker calibration).

Claire (CS): Closing loop with customer now. Will post final confirmation when they finish validation. :white_check_mark:
